title: ioctl_gen_iv: iv_set set even if set_iv fails after gen_iv succeeds
description: In ioctl_gen_iv(), the code calls gen_iv() to generate the IV, then calls set_iv() to program it into the provider session. If set_iv() fails, the goto goes to out_zeroize, which zeroizes the iv[] stack buffer and falls through to 'out:' — correctly not setting iv_set=true. The flow is: gen_iv() success → set_iv() failure → goto out_zeroize → memzero iv → mutex_unlock → return error. iv_set remains false. This is correct. HOWEVER: there is a subtle issue with the copy_to_user path. After set_iv() succeeds and memcpy(op.iv, iv, op.ivlen) is done, if copy_to_user fails, the function goes to out_zeroize without setting iv_set=true. This means: the IV IS programmed into the provider session (set_iv succeeded), but iv_set remains false. Subsequent write() calls will fail with -EINVAL because iv_set==false, even though the session actually has a valid IV. The session is in a partially-configured but unrecoverable state (can't call GEN_IV again without error since set_iv would program a DIFFERENT iv, can't call SET_IV to fix because caller doesn't know the generated IV bytes). Trigger: GEN_IV with valid ivlen but invalid uarg → set_iv succeeds (IV programmed in provider) → copy_to_user -EFAULT → iv_set=false → write() returns -EINVAL → session stuck.
